name: inputs-deep-merge-not-replace
query: We have `_envcommon/db.hcl` with `inputs = { tags = { team = "platform", env = "prod" } }`. In `envs/stg/db/terragrunt.hcl` we include it and set `inputs = { tags = { env = "stg" } }`, expecting the stg unit to have only `{ env = "stg" }`. Plan shows `{ team = "platform", env = "stg" }`. Where's the team tag coming from and how do we override the entire map?
expected_behavior: Explains the actual semantics: `inputs` is deep-merged across include + child. Scalars: child wins at the leaf. Nested maps: recursively merged, not replaced. So `tags.team` survives because the child never mentions it.
Names that the same rule applies to `mock_outputs`; whereas `remote_state` is shallow (child block overrides parent block entirely).

Gives two correct overrides: (a) restate every key in the child map so the merge produces the desired final state; (b) set `merge_strategy = "no_merge"` on the `include` block to skip merging the parent into the child entirely (loses everything inherited, not just the map).
Mentions the third option only if it fits: pre-compute tags in a `locals { }` block in the child and write `tags = local.tags` (sidesteps the deep-merge interaction).
Does NOT suggest setting parent keys to `null` in the child as a deletion mechanism — that does not delete in HCL deep-merge.
Does NOT recommend removing the include.
